claims.text: Ambient-temperature FeCoNiCrAl powder with a 15–45 μm particle-size distribution produces insufficient coating thickness.
In-line preheating of FeCoNiCrAl powder to 600–800°C will increase bond-coat thickness relative to ambient-temperature feedstock.
The thickness increase will occur without compromising coating integrity.
The thickness increase will occur without increasing as-sprayed oxidation.
Preheating causes the particles to reach a near- or fully molten state before impact.
Preheated particles form larger splats upon impact.
Preheated particles form more coherent splats upon impact.
Near- or complete melting promotes better splat cohesion.
Better melting and splat cohesion produce thicker individual deposits.
A controlled preheating history reduces the particles' tendency toward surface oxidation.
The elevated thermal energy supplied by preheating minimizes deleterious oxide-layer formation during flight.
Minimizing in-flight oxide formation preserves coating microstructure and adhesion.
The preheated-feedstock coating will retain robust mechanical cohesion in the as-sprayed state.
The intervention should remain effective under cyclic thermal-barrier-coating service exposure up to approximately 1200°C.
Nonuniform particle preheating can cause inconsistent melting, coating defects, or localized oxidation.
Particle overheating can cause inconsistent melting, coating defects, or localized oxidation.

contradictions.description: The baseline identifies 15–45 μm as the feedstock particle-size range, whereas the hypothesis and predicted outcome treat 15–45 μm as a baseline coating thickness to be exceeded. This conflates particle size with deposited coating thickness.
